nodes.name: N functionalization of carbon
nodes.procedure: 2 g of XC-72 carbon was homogeneously grinded with 3 g of urea. After which, the mixture was calcined at 150 °C for 2 h and 300 °C for another 4 h in a fully sealed crucible. The product was then washed sufficiently with water and dried at 60 °C overnight.
nodes.source_text: The N functionalized carbon supports were prepared according to our previous reports. Typically, 2 g of XC-72 carbon was homogeneously grinded with 3 g of urea...

nodes.name: CeO2 impregnation and reduction
nodes.procedure: 6 mg of Ce(NO3)3·6H2O were firstly added to 20 ml of deionized water and stirred to dissolve the Ce precursor. Subsequently, 0.1 g of NC support were added to the above solution. After further stirring for 12 h, the mixture was centrifugated and washed thoroughly, and the obtained solid products were dried at 60 °C overnight. At last, the obtained powders were reduced with hydrogen at 700 °C for 2 h.
nodes.source_text: The preparation of CeO2/NC was prepared via the impregnation method. To make it clear, 6 mg of Ce(NO3)3·6H2O were firstly added to 20 ml of deionized water...

nodes.name: Acid etching of CeO2/NC
nodes.procedure: The prepared CeO2/NC was then allowed for acid treatment (pH = 1) overnight. After sufficient washing and centrifugation, the obtained solid products were dried at 60 °C overnight to make the Ce1/NC catalyst.
nodes.source_text: The prepared CeO2/NC was then allowed for acid treatment (pH = 1) overnight...

nodes.name: Ce1·Run/NC synthesis
nodes.procedure: 2.5 mg of RuCl3 were dissolved in 10 ml of deionized water. After which, 0.058 g of Ce1/NC was added to the RuCl3 solution under mild stirring. After stirring for another 12 h, the mixture was sufficiently washed, and the obtained solid products were collected and dried at 60 °C overnight. Finally, the obtained powders were reduced at 250 °C for 2 h under hydrogen atmosphere.
nodes.source_text: Firstly, 2.5 mg of RuCl3 were dissolved in 10 ml of deionized water. After which, 0.058 g of Ce1/NC was added...

nodes.name: Run/NC synthesis
nodes.procedure: 2.5 mg of RuCl3 were added to 10 ml of deionized water and stirred to totally dissolve the Ru precursors. After which, 0.05 g of NC support were added to the RuCl3 solution under mild stirring. After further stirring for 12 h, the mixture was sufficiently centrifugated and washed. The obtained solid powders were collected and dried at 60 °C overnight. At last, the obtained powders were reduced with hydrogen at 250 °C for 2 h.
nodes.source_text: To begin with, 2.5 mg of RuCl3 were added to 10 ml of deionized water and stirred...

nodes.name: Ru1·Run/NC synthesis
nodes.procedure: The preparation of the Ru1·Run/NC catalyst was similar to that of the synthesis of the Run/NC catalyst. The only difference was that during the reduction of the Ru1·Run/NC catalyst, the reduction temperature was set at 180 °C.
nodes.source_text: The preparation of the Ru1·Run/NC catalyst was similar to that of the synthesis of the Run/NC catalyst...

nodes.name: Ru1/NC synthesis
nodes.procedure: A small amount of RuCl3 were dissolved in 10 ml of deionized water. Subsequently, 0.05 g of NC support were added to the solution and stirred for 12 h. After further centrifugation, the acquired solid powders were collected and dried at 60 °C overnight. Finally, the obtained powders were reduced with hydrogen at 180 °C for 2 h.
nodes.source_text: The synthesis of Ru1/NC catalyst was based on an impregnation method...

nodes.name: Run·CeO2/NC synthesis
nodes.procedure: 2.5 mg of RuCl3 were firstly added to 10 ml of deionized water under mild stirring. Subsequently, 0.05 g of CeO2/NC was added to the RuCl3 solution under stirring. After stirring for another 12 h, the mixture was thoroughly centrifugated and washed. The acquired solid products were then collected and dried at 60 °C overnight. After which, the obtained powders were reduced with hydrogen at 250 °C for 2 h.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ce loading 0.03 wt% in Ceᵧ/NC and Ce₁·Ruₙ/NC catalysts; Ru loading ~1 wt% in Ce₁·Ruₙ/NC and Ruₙ/NC catalysts as measured by ICP-OES (Table S1).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The loading amount of Ce in the Ce_y/NC catalyst was measured to be 0.03 wt% by an inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometer (ICP-OES) as displayed in Table S1... The Ru loading amounts of the Ce₁·Ruₙ/NC catalyst and the Ruₙ/NC catalyst were both about 1 wt% (Table S1) while the Ce weight loading in the Ce₁·Ruₙ/NC was 0.03 wt% as determined by the ICP-OES measurements.

nodes.characterization_summary: Only broad XRD peaks of carbon support observed for Ceᵧ/NC; no Ru diffraction peaks for Ruₙ/NC and Ce₁·Ruₙ/NC due to ultrasmall Ru nanoclusters.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Due to the low Ce loadings, only the broad X-ray diffraction (XRD) peaks of carbon support were observed for the Ce_y/NC catalyst as displayed in Fig. S4... No diffraction peaks of Ru were identified for both of the Ruₙ/NC catalyst and the Ce₁·Ruₙ/NC catalyst as shown in Fig. S8.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ruₙ/NC shows fully-exposed Ru nanoclusters with average size 1.1±0.3 nm evenly dispersed; Ce₁·Ruₙ/NC shows mean Ru nanocluster size 1.0±0.2 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As presented by the HAADF-STEM images of the Ruₙ/NC catalyst in Fig. 2i–k, fully-exposed Ruₙ nanoclusters with an average particle size of 1.1±0.3 nm were evenly dispersed on its NC support... The AC HAADF-STEM images of the Ce₁·Ruₙ/NC catalyst in Fig. 2p–r showed that the mean particle size of the fullyexposed Ru nanoclusters in it was 1.0±0.2 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ce species atomically dispersed in Ceᵧ/NC and Ce₁·Ruₙ/NC; Ru nanoclusters confirmed in Ce₁·Ruₙ/NC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As was further revealed by the aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM (AC HAADF-STEM) measurement, Ce species were atomically dispersed in the Ce/NC catalyst (Fig. 2b–d)... The AC HAADF-STEM images of the Ce₁·Ruₙ/NC catalyst in Fig. 2p–r showed that the mean particle size of the fully-exposed Ru nanoclusters in it was 1.0±0.2 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Uniform dispersion of Ce in Ceᵧ/NC; Ru concentrated on nanoclusters and Ce as single atoms in Ce₁·Ruₙ/NC; Ru elemental nature confirmed in Ruₙ/NC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Corresponding energy-dispersive X-ray spectrometry (EDS) elementary mapping images of the Ce_y/NC catalyst in Fig. 2e–g also confirmed the uniform dispersion of Ce species in it... Corresponding EDS elementary mapping images of the Ce₁·Ruₙ/NC catalyst... indicated that the Ru element signal was concentrated on the small nanoclusters while the Ce element signal was highly overlapped with the distribution of single atoms.

nodes.characterization_summary: Edge absorption energies of Ce₁·Ruₙ/NC and Ruₙ/NC between Ru foil and RuO₂ indicate Ru oxidation states between 0 and +4; Ce₁·Ruₙ/NC shows negative shift relative to Ruₙ/NC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 3a shows the near-edge XAFS spectra (XANES) at Ru K-edge of the Ce₁·Ruₙ/NC catalyst, Ruₙ/NC catalyst and reference Ru foil and RuO₂. It was displayed by the enlarged Ru K-edge XANES spectra in the inset of Fig. 3a that the edge absorption energies of the Ce₁·Ruₙ/NC catalyst and Ruₙ/NC catalyst were between Ru foil and RuO₂... the edge energy of the Ce₁·Ruₙ/NC catalyst showed a negative shift relative to the Ruₙ/NC catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru-N coordination dominant over Ru-Ru (CN~2) in both Ce₁·Ruₙ/NC and Ruₙ/NC; increased Ru-N ratio due to small particle size.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The best fitted Fourier transforms of the Ru K-edge extended XAFS (EXAFS) spectrum... the mean Ru-Ru coordination number of the Ruₙ/NC catalyst was about 2... The Fourier transforms of the Ru K-edge EXAFS oscillations... presented a main coordination peak below 2 Å, matching to the Ru-N coordination.

nodes.characterization_summary: Single atom nature of Ce confirmed in Ce₁·Ruₙ/NC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ce LIII-edge XANES and fitted EXAFS spectra of the Ce₁·Ruₙ/NC catalyst... again indicated the single atom nature of Ce species in the Ce₁·Ruₙ/NC catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: No Ce-Ce coordination; Ce-C coordination at 3.2 Å confirms atomic dispersion of Ce.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As indicated by the Fourier transforms of the Ce LIII-edge EXAFS spectra in Fig. 3g, a coordination peak at 3.8 Å was identified for the reference CeO₂... the Ce₁·Ruₙ/NC catalyst presented a coordination peak at 3.2 Å that was markedly shorter than that of the Ce-Ce coordination.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru 3p binding energy negatively shifted in Ce₁·Ruₙ/NC vs Ruₙ/NC due to electron back-donation from Ce.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electron transfer between Ce single atoms and Ru nanoclusters... was further evidenced by the Ru 3p XPS spectra in Fig. 3h, wherein the Ru⁰ binding energy peak of the Ce₁·Ruₙ/NC catalyst was slightly negatively shifted compared with the Ruₙ/NC catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ce₁·Ruₙ/NC shows stronger OH-desorption peak intensity around 0.60-1.00 V and negative peak shift vs Ruₙ/NC, indicating enhanced OH adsorption.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 4a displayed that the OH-desorption peak intensity around 0.60-1.00 V of the Ce₁·Ruₙ/NC catalyst was much stronger than that of the Ruₙ/NC catalyst... the OH desorption peak of the Ce₁·Ruₙ/NC catalyst also displayed a negative shift relative to that of the Ruₙ/NC catalyst.
